text.p: Colombian stocks eked out modest gains as investors with year-end cash surpluses poured money into stocks for tax purposes, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.11 percent to close at 13,318.21 on active trading of 2.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB ended up for the eighth consecutive day, closing with a 0.20 percent gain at 843.69 on a volume of 1.09 billion.
"The market is very liquid and some people are investing their year-end surpluses in small packages of shares," one broker said.

He spoke on the sidelines of Monday's National Stockbrokers Meeting in Bogota where industry officials generally said they were anxious to get 1996 -- a poor year for equities -- behind them and move toward hopeful recovery in 1997.
Volume in Bogota was partly fueled by a large cross trade in cigarette maker Coltabaco, which ended unchanged at 3,000 pesos per share, brokers said.
They said brewer Bavaria SA, which ended up 0.25 percent at 4,00 pesos per share, was also heavily traded, with nearly 280 million pesos of shares trading hands.

A full 1.6 billion pesos of the volume in Medellin was concentrated in confeccioner Compaia Nacional de Chocolates. It closed up a barely noticeable 0.01 percent, however, ending 8,301 pesos per share.

Coltabaco, also active in Medellin, ended unchanged at 3,000 as did cement manufacturer Cementos Argos, which accounted for more than 256 million pesos of total volume, but ended stable at 5,300 pesos a share.
